The work function is the **minimum** energy needed to free an electron from the metal
surface.
**Step 1 — state the definition.** φ is the **least** energy an electron must acquire
to escape the metal ✓ Electrons at the top of the conduction band are the most loosely
bound, and φ is measured from that level to the vacuum.
**Step 2 — see where it appears.** In Einstein's photoelectric equation,
**KE_max = hν − φ** ✓
A photon of energy **less** than φ ejects nothing, however many arrive.
**Why "minimum" is the key word.** Electrons deeper in the metal need **more** than φ ✓
Those emerge with less kinetic energy, which is why photoelectrons have a whole
**spread** of speeds up to the maximum hν − φ.
**The threshold conditions.**
threshold frequency: **ν₀ = φ/h** ✓
threshold wavelength: **λ₀ = hc/φ** ✓
Below ν₀ - or above λ₀ - there is no emission at all.
**Typical values.**
caesium: **2·1 eV** ✓ the lowest of the common metals, which is why it is used in
photocells sensitive to visible light
sodium: 2·3 eV
zinc: 4·3 eV
platinum: **6·4 eV** ✓ needing ultraviolet
**Why φ varies between metals.** It depends on how tightly the lattice binds its
conduction electrons ✓ and also on the **surface** condition: a trace of oxide or
adsorbed gas can change φ by a volt or more, which is why photoelectric experiments
demand clean surfaces.
**Why the sharp threshold matters historically.** Classical wave theory predicted that
**any** frequency would work given enough intensity or time ✓ The observed threshold,
and the instantaneous emission above it, could only be explained by Einstein's photon
hypothesis of 1905 - for which he received the Nobel Prize.
**What determines the number of electrons.** The **intensity** ✓ not the work
function. φ fixes **whether** emission occurs and **how fast** the electrons emerge;
intensity fixes **how many**.
**The related quantity.** The **stopping potential**, eV₀ = hν − φ ✓ Plotting V₀
against ν gives a straight line of slope h/e and intercept −φ/e - Millikan's
measurement of Planck's constant.
**Reading the distractors.** "**Maximum possible energy acquired**" ✗ describes
KE_max. "**Equal for all metals**" ✗ is plainly false. "**Maximum energy given to move
out**" ✗ reverses "minimum" ✓
∴ Minimum energy required by an electron to just eject from metal surface.

Match each of **Maxwell's four equations** to the law it expresses.
**Step 1 — Gauss's law for electrostatics.**
∮Ē·d̄Ā = **Q/ε₀** ✓ → **(i)**
The electric flux through a closed surface is set by the charge enclosed - electric
field lines begin and end on charges.
**Step 2 — Gauss's law for magnetism.**
∮B̄·d̄Ā = **0** ✓ → **(iii)**
The magnetic flux through any closed surface is **zero**, because no magnetic
**monopole** exists. Magnetic field lines always close on themselves.
**Step 3 — Faraday's law.**
∮Ē·d̄l̄ = **−dΦ_B/dt** ✓ → **(iv)**
A changing magnetic flux induces an electric field - the basis of the generator, the
transformer and the induction motor. The minus sign is **Lenz's law**.
**Step 4 — the Ampere-Maxwell law.**
∮B̄·d̄l̄ = µ₀[i_c + ε₀ dΦ_E/dt] ✓ → **(ii)**
A magnetic field is produced by a conduction current **and** by a changing electric
flux - Maxwell's **displacement current**.
**Step 5 — assemble.** **a-i, b-iii, c-iv, d-ii** ✓
**Maxwell's great addition.** The displacement-current term ✓ Without it, Ampere's law
fails for a charging capacitor: no conduction current crosses the gap, yet a magnetic
field surrounds it. The changing electric flux supplies what is missing.
**Why that term changed physics.** Adding it made the equations **self-consistent**
and predicted **electromagnetic waves** travelling at
c = 1/√(µ₀ε₀) ✓ which matched the measured speed of light - and so revealed that light
is an electromagnetic wave.
**The symmetry of the four.** Two are **flux** laws over closed surfaces; two are
**circulation** laws round closed loops ✓ The only asymmetry is the zero on the right
of the magnetic Gauss law - the signature of the missing monopole.
**How to recognise each at sight.**
a closed **surface** integral of **E** → Gauss for electricity ✓
a closed **surface** integral of **B** → Gauss for magnetism, always zero ✓
a **loop** integral of **E** → Faraday ✓
a **loop** integral of **B** → Ampere-Maxwell ✓
**What they encompass.** Together with the Lorentz force, these four equations contain
the whole of classical electromagnetism ✓ - every circuit, every motor, every radio
wave and the whole of optics.
∴ a − i, b − iii, c − iv, d − ii.

Read the three angles from the figure using the **law of reflection**.
**Step 1 — the angle of reflection.** The incident ray makes **30°** with the normal,
and by the law of reflection the reflected ray makes the same angle:
angle of reflection = **30°** → **(iii)** ✓
**Step 2 — the angle α.** It is measured from the **surface**, not the normal ✓ Since
the normal is perpendicular to the surface,
α = 90° − 30°
= **60°** → **(i)** ✓
**Step 3 — the angle of deviation.** The ray would have continued straight on; instead
it leaves on the other side of the normal:
δ = 180° − 2i
= 180° − 60°
= **120°** → **(ii)** ✓
**Step 4 — assemble.** **a-iii, b-i, c-ii** ✓
**The law of reflection, stated fully.**
the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection ✓
the incident ray, the reflected ray and the normal all lie in **one plane** ✓
Both parts are needed to fix the reflected ray completely.
**Why angles are measured from the normal.** It makes the laws of reflection **and**
refraction take their simplest forms ✓ Snell's law in terms of grazing angles would be
clumsy, and the two conventions would clash. The glancing angle α is given here
precisely to test whether that convention is known.
**Checking the deviation formula.**
normal incidence, i = 0: δ = **180°** ✓ the ray comes straight back
grazing, i = 90°: δ = **0°** ✓ it skims past undeviated
i = 45°: δ = **90°** ✓ a right-angle turn, which is why 45° mirrors are used in
periscopes
Here i = 30° gives **120°** ✓
**The angle between the incident and reflected rays.** 2i = **60°** ✓ which is **not**
the deviation - the deviation is its supplement. Confusing the two is the commonest
error, and 60° appears among the options for exactly that reason.
**Why the deviation exceeds 90° here.** The incidence is **shallow** relative to the
normal, so the ray is turned back sharply ✓ The smaller the angle of incidence, the
greater the deviation.
**Why reflection is specular.** The surface is smooth compared with the wavelength, so
a parallel beam stays parallel ✓ A rough surface scatters diffusely and no single
deviation can be quoted.
∴ a − iii, b − i, c − ii.

Rearrange Coulomb's law for ε₀ and read off the units.
**Step 1 — start from Coulomb's law.**
F = q₁q₂/(4πε₀r²) ✓
**Step 2 — solve for ε₀.**
ε₀ = q₁q₂/(4πFr²) ✓
**Step 3 — substitute the units.**
= (C x C)/(N x m²)
= **C² m⁻² N⁻¹** ✓
**The numerical value.**
ε₀ = **8·854 x 10⁻¹² C² m⁻² N⁻¹** ✓
**The equivalent unit.** C² N⁻¹ m⁻² is the same as **farad per metre** ✓
From C = ε₀A/d, ε₀ = Cd/A has units F m/m² = **F m⁻¹** - which is how ε₀ is usually
quoted in engineering, as 8·854 pF m⁻¹.
**What ε₀ represents.** The **permittivity of free space** ✓ a measure of how much
electric field a given charge produces in vacuum - or, equivalently, of how readily
space "permits" an electric field.
**Its partner constant.**
µ₀ = **4π x 10⁻⁷ T m A⁻¹** ✓ and together they fix the speed of light:
c = 1/√(µ₀ε₀) = **3 x 10⁸ m s⁻¹** ✓ one of the great results of nineteenth-century
physics.
**Why the 4π appears in Coulomb's law.** It is **rationalisation** ✓ Putting the 4π
into the force law removes it from Gauss's law and from the field equations, where it
would otherwise clutter every expression. The geometry of a sphere is where it comes
from.
**The dimensional formula.**
[ε₀] = **[M⁻¹ L⁻³ T⁴ A²]** ✓ since C = A s.
**Where ε₀ appears elsewhere.**
Gauss's law: ∮Ē·d̄Ā = q/ε₀ ✓
parallel-plate capacitor: C = ε₀A/d ✓
energy density: u = ½ε₀E² ✓
the speed of light, as above ✓
**In a medium.** ε = ε₀ε_r, with ε_r the **dielectric constant** ✓ which is 1 for
vacuum, about 1·0006 for air, 80 for water.
**Reading the distractors.** **C² m² N⁻¹** ✗ has the length power the wrong way round.
**C⁻¹ m² N⁻²** ✗ and **C² m² N²** ✗ invert the charge or the force ✓ Rearranging
Coulomb's law settles it in one line.
∴ C² m⁻² N⁻¹.

A gang capacitor is a set of parallel-plate capacitors **in parallel**, one for each
gap.
**Step 1 — find the capacitance of a single gap.**
C₁ = ε₀A/d ✓
with A = 5 cm² = **5 x 10⁻⁴ m²** and d = 0·885 cm = **8·85 x 10⁻³ m**:
C₁ = (8·85 x 10⁻¹²)(5 x 10⁻⁴)/(8·85 x 10⁻³) ✓
**Step 2 — evaluate.**
= (8·85 x 5/8·85) x 10⁻¹²⁻⁴⁺³
= 5 x 10⁻¹³ F
= **0·5 pF** ✓
**Step 3 — count the gaps.** Interlocking plates form **one capacitor per gap**, and
for n plates there are **n − 1** gaps ✓ The arrangement shown provides **8** of them.
**Step 4 — combine in parallel.** Parallel capacitances **add**:
C = 8 x 0·5
= **4 pF** ✓
**Why the gaps are in parallel.** Alternate plates are connected together, so every gap
shares the **same** pair of terminals ✓ and the same voltage appears across each.
**Why this is the standard way to make a large capacitance.** Interleaving multiplies
the effective area without increasing the bulk ✓ A variable gang capacitor in an old
radio tuner used dozens of plates, rotating one set to vary the **overlap** and so the
capacitance.
**Why the 8·85 is chosen.** It cancels the 8·85 in ε₀ ✓ leaving the clean 5 x 10⁻¹³ F -
a sure sign the examiner intended the arithmetic to come out exactly.
**How such a capacitor is tuned.** Rotating the moving plates changes the **overlapping
area A** ✓ so the capacitance varies continuously - which is how a radio set selects a
station, by shifting the resonant frequency 1/(2π√LC).
**The general formula.**
C = **(n − 1)ε₀A/d** ✓ for n interleaved plates of overlap area A.
**A check on the magnitude.** Picofarads are typical for air-spaced capacitors of this
size ✓ Reaching microfarads requires a thin dielectric film and a very large rolled
area.
**Why air and not a dielectric.** Air lets the plates move freely for tuning, and its
losses are negligible ✓ The price is a small capacitance, since ε_r = 1.
**Reading the distractors.** **0·5 pF** would be a single gap, and is not offered;
**1·06**, **6·36** and **12·72 pF** ✗ correspond to no whole number of 0·5 pF gaps ✓
∴ 4 PF.

Impulse is **force x time**, which has the dimensions of **momentum**.
**Step 1 — write the definition.**
J = **FΔt** ✓
**Step 2 — substitute the dimensions.**
[J] = [M L T⁻²][T]
= **[M L T⁻¹]** ✓
**Step 3 — recognise it.** Those are exactly the dimensions of **momentum**, mv ✓
**Why that is no coincidence.** The **impulse-momentum theorem** states
J = **Δp** ✓
Impulse is not merely dimensionally like momentum - it **equals** the change in
momentum, which follows directly from Newton's second law:
F = dp/dt, so ∫F dt = Δp ✓
**The SI unit.** **N s**, equivalently **kg m s⁻¹** ✓ The two are the same, as the
dimensions require.
**Why impulse is the useful quantity in collisions.** The force during an impact varies
wildly and is almost impossible to measure ✓ but its **time integral** - the impulse -
is simply the measurable change in momentum. One need never know the detailed force
history.
**A worked instance.** A 0·15 kg ball striking a bat at 35 m s⁻¹ and rebounding at the
same speed:
J = 0·15(70) = **10·5 N s** ✓
and if the contact lasts 1 ms, the average force is **10500 N** - about a tonne-weight.
**The practical application.** Extending Δt **reduces** the force for the same
impulse ✓ Airbags, crash helmets, landing mats, crumple zones and the bending of the
knees on landing all work this way: the momentum change is fixed, so lengthening the
time is the only way to soften the blow.
**The graphical meaning.** Impulse is the **area under the force-time graph** ✓ which
is why a tall narrow spike and a low broad hump can deliver the same impulse.
**Why it is a vector.** It has the direction of the force, and of the momentum change ✓
In two dimensions the components must be treated separately.
**Reading the distractors.** **M L⁻¹ T⁻¹** ✗ and **M L⁻¹ T** ✗ have the length power
negative, which no force-times-time can give. **M⁻¹ L T⁻¹** ✗ inverts the mass ✓
Checking against momentum, mv = [M][L T⁻¹], settles it at once.
∴ MLT⁻¹.
